tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Writes text or code directly to a file on disk in the workspace with UTF-8 encoding. Use this to create or overwrite complete files (Python scripts, HTML, CSS, React components, JSON, etc.).

file_path.description: Path to the file to create or overwrite (e.g. 'src/App.jsx' or 'index.html')

content.description: Complete text/code content to write to the file

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Surgical search-and-replace editor: Replaces exact target_text with replacement_text in a file. Preserves all other code, structure, and comments without rewriting the whole file.

file_path.description: Path to the file to edit

target_text.description: Exact text/lines to find and replace

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Reads the text contents of a file in the workspace.

file_path.description: Path to the file to read

tools.name: list_directory
tools.description: Lists files and subdirectories in a workspace folder with tree depth control (e.g. to inspect codebase structure).

tools.name: grep_search
tools.description: Fast regex and text code search across all source files in the workspace (finds definitions, usages, imports).

is_regex.description: True if query is a regular expression

tools.name: run_terminal_command
tools.description: Direct Terminal / Shell Access: Executes bash, powershell, or cmd terminal commands directly on the host system without asking for confirmation. Use this to install dependencies, run builds, launch servers, run tests, or execute scripts.

command.description: The exact shell command to execute in the terminal

tools.name: fetch_url
tools.description: Fetches and extracts clean readable text from a URL (useful for real-time library documentation, API specs, and online guides).

tools.name: google_search
tools.description: Google search tool to query the web for real-time information, documentation, and answers.

tools.name: self_tool_creator
tools.description: Autonomous Self Tool Creator: Call this tool whenever you need a tool/function that does not exist yet. You provide the python function code, function name, and description. It will automatically write to tools.py, register in tools_list.json, and hot-reload it into active memory so you can immediately use it.

tool_name.description: Unique python function name (e.g. calculate_math, fetch_weather)

description.description: Clear description of what the new tool does and how to call it

python_code.description: Complete Python function definition e.g. def calculate_math(expression: str) -> str: ...

parameters_json_str.description: Optional JSON schema string for parameters

tools.name: git_status
tools.description: Shows current git repository status: staged changes, unstaged modifications, and untracked files. Use before committing to understand the current state.

tools.name: git_diff
tools.description: Shows the git diff (file changes) in the repository. Set staged=true to see what would be committed (staged diff). Default shows unstaged working tree changes.

staged.description: If true, shows staged diff (what would be committed). Default false shows working tree diff.

tools.name: git_commit
tools.description: Stages all current changes and creates a git commit. Automatically generates a Conventional Commits message if none is provided (feat/fix/refactor/chore etc).

message.description: Commit message. If empty, auto-generates from diff analysis.

tools.name: git_push
tools.description: Pushes the current branch to the remote origin repository.

branch.description: Branch name to push. Defaults to current branch.

tools.name: git_create_pr
tools.description: Creates a GitHub Pull Request via the gh CLI. Automatically pushes the branch first. Requires gh CLI to be installed and authenticated.

title.description: PR title. Auto-generated from diff if empty.

base.description: Base branch to merge into (default: main).
